interpretation: This packet records first-party SVEP observations for reviewer use. It does not establish that a particular State, district or block is covered, create a universal applicant entitlement, approve finance, or authorize publication.
sourcePolicy: The official SVEP portal, official FAQ, contact route and Ministry of Rural Development context are primary. State/block coverage, local intake, community implementation, finance, repayment, documents and current operating terms must be verified for the applicant's location. UdyamVeda can prepare a profile and checklist but cannot create a local SVEP entitlement or impersonate a community implementation user.

records.sourceAnchor: SVEP objective, DAY-NRLM relationship, early-stage rural enterprises, community implementation model, support categories and current portal update
observations: The official portal describes SVEP as part of DAY-NRLM, a centrally sponsored programme implemented since June 2011; it records approval as an NRLM sub-scheme in May 2015 and guidelines issued on 15 June 2015. The portal was last updated on 19 January 2026.

SVEP is intended to help rural poor establish and stabilise enterprises, particularly early-stage and new non-farm enterprises, through a combination of financial assistance, business-management and soft-skills training, business-development support, mentoring, finance access, banking linkage and convergence guidance.

The delivery model uses State/block implementation structures and community cadres or enterprise-support institutions. The FAQ describes profile, business-plan and related data workflows; it is not a general public national self-service loan application.

The official portal does not establish one universal applicant-level grant, loan ceiling, fee, repayment term or national deadline. Applicable finance and support terms depend on the covered State/block and local implementation route.

Eligibility therefore requires a rural location in an active SVEP implementation area, an eligible proposed or existing non-farm enterprise and the applicable State/block/community process. Unknown block coverage must produce more-information-required, not automatic ineligibility.

The programme focuses on rural self-employment and small enterprises, with particular attention to youth, women and skill-based work, but the portal's programme description does not replace local eligibility or implementation confirmation.

The portal disclaimer directs users to verify information with the relevant State Rural Livelihoods Mission or government department. UdyamVeda must present SVEP as local, conditional support rather than a guaranteed cash benefit.
reviewFollowUps: Verify the applicant's State, district and block against the current SVEP implementation route and identify the authorized local contact or enterprise-support channel.
Confirm current intake, eligible activities, profile/business-plan documents, finance mechanism, contribution, repayment, training, mentoring and service timeline for that route.
Keep financial assistance, training, mentoring, banking linkage and convergence as separate benefit buckets; do not invent a national loan or grant ceiling.
Check current portal and FAQ revisions, local notices and any State/block supersession before publication.
Record amendment or supersession evidence and obtain a reviewer decision before publication.

publicationGuard.reason: Official SVEP evidence supports the programme purpose and support model, but local State/block coverage, current intake, finance terms, documents, implementation route and human approval remain unresolved.
